meaning: The number 30,000 appears in several biblical contexts but has no independently established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: The number 30000 is mentioned, among other places, in 1 Samuel 4:10, where 30000 Israelite foot soldiers fell in battle against the Philistines, and in 1 Samuel 13:5, where the Philistines gathered 30000 chariots. It is used primarily as a large, round number to express military strength or great loss, rather than as a number with deep symbolic or mystical meaning. In Jewish numerology (gematria) and rabbinic tradition, 30000 is not attributed any special independent symbolism beyond being a multiple of 3 and 10, which each carry symbolic weight on their own.
